_note: Pepin's own voice loop, the cascade (scripts/voice_cascade.py, pepin.voice_cascade): local ears (loudness gate + Whisper on the Mac) -> Claude as the talker (streamed, prompt-cached, the robot's tools) -> local voice (Qwen3-TTS on the Mac) -> the board's speaker. Every key can be switched for one run with --set section.key=value. Costs are ESTIMATES from the prices below and the API's own token counts.

ears.note: wake name: a conversation opens only on the robot's name (pepin.voice_live.wake.is_wake); always: every utterance is a turn (the bench). silence_s: the end of the turn is this much quiet after the last loud frame (0.4 s; 0.5 s was the Live gate's). 2026-10-09, 18 of Artem's live utterances with 0.25 s of quiet inserted mid-sentence (scratch/voice_cascade_eot/eot_eval.py): silence 0.5 closed 2-3 of them early, 0.4 3-4, Smart Turn 0.5 15-16, Smart Turn 0.85 13-15; with the continuation merge none stayed cut (the voice always came back within 0.8 s); the close after the last word: 500, 400, 220 (max 500), 220 (max 400 with silence 0.4) ms. start_db: a frame this far above the room's floor is voice. floor_min_dbfs: the floor never follows the room below this (-85: the XVF3800's noise suppression delivers -90..-94 dBFS between words, 2026-10-09 logs, so a higher floor would call quiet syllables silence; macOS say pads with digital silence; a floor that low opened the gate on -84 dBFS hiss for 15 s at a time, read by Whisper as 'Продолжение следует...'); speech sits at -50..-20 dBFS. continuation_s: the person starting again this soon after an utterance closed (by the model or the silence), before any of the reply was played, cancels the brain's call and the two utterances become one turn (2026-10-09: Smart Turn closed 'сегодня день.' at p 0.97 and the rest of the sentence came as the next turn); 0: off. Once the reply plays, it is a barge-in (flags.barge_in). turn_model: null (the fixed silence alone) or smart-turn-v3.2 (the turn section)

turn.note: with ears.turn_model smart-turn-v3.2 (pipecat-ai/smart-turn-v3, smart-turn-v3.2-cpu.onnx: 8 MB int8 ONNX on the CPU, BSD-2-Clause, 23 languages with Russian at 93.5 % on its own benchmark; ~9 ms a call here): at min_silence_s of quiet inside an utterance the model reads its last window_s seconds (zeros in front, as it was trained) on a worker thread, and the utterance closes when it says p >= threshold (0.85: at 0.5 it cut 'сегодня день.' live at p 0.97, and at either it fires in most 0.25 s mid-sentence pauses, which the continuation merge joins back); otherwise ears.silence_s closes it as before. Every turn logs p, the model's own ms and the time saved against the fixed silence

transcriber.note: Whisper turbo on the Mac's GPU, ~0.26 s a phrase; Russian forced. early_s: Whisper starts on an utterance at this much quiet inside it, while the end-of-turn silence is still running, so its words are ready when the utterance closes (0: only after the close). A call costs ~230 ms whatever the length (the 30 s encoder window: 0.5 s of audio 233 ms, 5 s 299 ms, 8 s 326 ms on the M5, 2026-10-09), so decoding only the tail would not get under it; a pause the person talks through wastes one call. Its noise lines (subtitle credits, a bare 'Спасибо.') are dropped (pepin.voice_live.wake.is_hallucination)

brain.note: preset picks model + thinking + effort; keys beside it win (--set brain.effort=medium). Thinking off: Haiku 5.5 'disabled'; Sonnet 5.5 'between_tools' (it refuses 'disabled'); Opus 5.5 cannot switch thinking off, 'adaptive' + effort low is its floor. Measured first word with a ~3k-token cached persona: Haiku 0.56 s, Sonnet 0.64 s, Opus 2.3 s; a tool round trip adds 1.4 s (Haiku) to 3.4 s (Sonnet). Gemini (provider gemini, GEMINI_API_KEY): thinking off is the lowest each model takes, probed 2026-10-09: 3.5 Flash-Lite refuses thinking_budget 0, takes thinking_level minimal; 3.5 Flash takes budget 0; 3.8 Flash takes budget 0 but still thinks (56 tokens on a greeting) and refuses minimal, so level low; its implicit cache needs a 4096-token prefix and has no write premium; keep_warm_s 0 (a warm-up would re-bill the whole prefix). cache: a breakpoint on the persona (tools + persona, shared by every conversation) and on the growing conversation; prewarm: a max_tokens 0 call at start writes it, and again after keep_warm_s without a call (the cache lives 5 min). The key: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment

voice.note: qwen3: Qwen3-TTS 0.6B CustomVoice through mlx-audio 0.5.8, loaded once on its own thread and kept hot; streams chunk_s chunks, first audio ~0.11 s warm (2.2 s cold: warmed at load), ~0.4x real time. chunk_s 0.2 (2026-10-09, 1 to 15 words, 5 runs each): first chunk 61-115 ms against 185-203 ms at 0.5, with 0.07 s or more of audio always queued ahead of the speaker (no gap); the first chunk barely depends on the sentence's length. hf_home: an HF cache already holding the weights (relative to the main checkout); missing there, the default cache is used. openers: the commonest first sentences, synthesised at load and played from memory when the brain says one (no TTS wait). say: macOS say, whole sentences at 16 kHz, for a test without the model

player.note: the pacer runs lead_s ahead of the speaker in block_s blocks: the jitter buffer over WiFi (0.5 s, as the Live loop), and what a barge-in has to silence (the board flushes it). It does not delay the first sample: the first block goes at once

flags.note: barge_in: while Pepin speaks, a voice over the barge_in threshold for hold_s flushes the speaker at once and cuts the conversation to what was heard; the person's words become the next turn (off: the mic is shut while Pepin speaks, as in the Live loop). backchannel: a short local clip when the person pauses mid-utterance. prosody_tags: Praat's numbers against the running baseline as a tag line in front of the person's words

barge_in.note: a frame is a voice cutting in when it stands over_floor_db above the room's floor and at least min_dbfs; the echo of the robot's own voice sits ~40 dB under the person's (XVF3800 echo cancellation). Every turn logs echo_peak_db (the loudest frame while the reply played) and every utterance voice_peak_db: set these from those two

backchannel.note: a clip (synthesised once at load) when the person has been quiet delay_s inside an utterance of at least min_speech_s, before the end of the turn

prosody.speaker: Артём
prosody.note: the tag line names speaker (no speaker ID yet), says nothing until min_baseline utterances are in the running baseline (the last window of this run), and gives a word for each number at least z of the person's spreads from their mean (2.0: Artem's deliberate contrasts sit at 2.7-6 sd, and with five numbers z 1.0 flagged 8 of the 10 tagged phrases of the 2026-10-08 bench): loudness, rate (syllables/s), pitch (median, st), intonation (5-95 % range, st), long pauses. emotion_model: null, audeering (arousal joins the numbers; CC-BY-NC-SA research weights, 0.7 GB) or emotion2vec (its label quoted; needs funasr installed). scratch/prosody_1008/REPORT.md: the plain numbers separate Artem's deliberate contrasts by 2.7-6 sd; the label models contradict each other

conversation.note: tool_filler: said locally (a clip made at load) when the brain calls a slow tool (see, look, find...) before saying a word in its reply; empty: off. a conversation closes after idle_close_s without the person's voice or a reply (never while a drive runs), on a goodbye, on end_conversation, or at max_session_s. report_drive_start: a drive answers its call when the goal server takes it (the brain says its acknowledgement) and its end comes as a [robot] turn. error_line: said locally when the brain fails before saying anything

prices_usd_per_mtok.note: Anthropic list prices (the claude-api reference, cached 2026-10-06): cache reads 0.1x input (0.05x on Opus 5.5), 5-minute cache writes 1.25x. Haiku 5.5 prompts over 100k tokens cost more (never reached here). Gemini (the coordinator's figures, 2026-10-09): cached input at the cached rate, no write premium

money.note: a conversation that would break a cap is never opened; the estimates are kept in data/voice/cascade_ledger.jsonl
